key_insight: Wall-bounded turbulence can sustain and regenerate even when all structures longer than about \u03bb_x^+ \u2248 600 are damped, implying that long streaks are not essential for turbulence survival.
engineering_relevance: This suggests smaller, finite-domain simulations may capture the essential near-wall self-sustaining physics, reducing computational cost for turbulence modeling and CFD design.
method: Damped long streaks while monitoring whether turbulence regrew.
Damped long rollers independently to test which structures were necessary for persistence.
Applied simultaneous damping of both streaks and rollers longer than \u03bb_x^+ \u2248 600 and analyzed the resulting energy balance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments and simulations showing turbulence persistence and recovery under selective damping, with regeneration observed after the damping is removed.
watch_item: The conclusions are drawn from a specific damping wavelength and idealized flow setup, so generalization to broader wall-turbulent configurations should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Wall-bounded turbulence needs not be long
